question: A 26-year-old woman with confirmed PID is assessed for management. Which of the following features would be the STRONGEST indication for hospital admission and IV antibiotics rather than outpatient oral treatment?

answers.text: Mild bilateral adnexal tenderness with cervical motion tenderness and no systemic features

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Mild PID without systemic features or surgical emergency is appropriate for outpatient oral antibiotic treatment (e.g., IM ceftriaxone + oral doxycycline + metronidazole). Hospital admission is not required for uncomplicated mild PID.

answers.text: Pelvic ultrasound showing a 6 cm tubo-ovarian abscess with fever and rigors

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A tubo-ovarian abscess (TOA) is the most important indication for hospital admission and IV antibiotics in PID. A TOA >5 cm, presence of fever/rigors, failure of outpatient treatment, inability to tolerate oral medication, and surgical emergency (rupture) are all indications for admission. TOA requires IV antibiotics and may need surgical/radiological drainage.

answers.text: Positive NAAT for Chlamydia trachomatis on cervical swab with mild pelvic pain

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A positive chlamydia NAAT indicates infection but does not by itself mandate hospital admission. Uncomplicated chlamydial PID can be treated with oral doxycycline plus metronidazole as an outpatient if systemic features and TOA are absent.

answers.text: Elevated CRP and ESR with no sonographic abnormality

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR) are additional supportive criteria for PID diagnosis but do not independently mandate admission in the absence of a TOA, systemic instability, or surgical emergency. Most women with mildly elevated markers and no complex adnexal mass can be managed as outpatients.

overallFeedback.feedback: Indications for PID admission: TOA, surgical emergency (ruptured TOA), severe systemic illness (high fever, rigors), failure of outpatient therapy, inability to tolerate oral antibiotics, pregnancy, uncertain diagnosis, immunosuppression.

Correct. TOA is the key indication for admission. Other indications: surgical emergency, severe systemic illness, failure of outpatient treatment, inability to tolerate oral medication, pregnancy, immunodeficiency.
